name: Daniel González
headline: Clarity through complexity.
intro: I connect systems, product decisions and people. My focus: dependable software, thoughtful interfaces and teams that can move with confidence.

projects.title: Across architectures.
projects.name: Prisma
projects.summary: Exploring the boundary between machine instructions and portable execution.
projects.problem: How can a binary built for one instruction set execute on another while preserving its behavior?
projects.approach: The repository separates decoding, an intermediate representation, optimization, emission and runtime responsibilities. That decomposition makes each boundary inspectable.
projects.tradeoff: Translation performance competes with correctness and compatibility. A staged pipeline makes validation explicit, while adding intermediate structures and engineering complexity.
projects.outcome: The public repository contains the translation pipeline, a formal specification area and a Rust migration. It is an evolving research project, not a claim of complete application compatibility.
projects.lesson: Ambitious systems benefit from small, testable contracts between stages. The most useful artifact is often the boundary that makes a failure understandable.

projects.title: Carefully connected.
projects.name: Clinic platform
projects.summary: Connecting appointments, inventory and purchasing in a deliberately bounded product demo.
projects.problem: Clinic workflows cross several operational boundaries. A useful demonstration must show those connections without suggesting it is ready for real patient care.
projects.approach: The project separates the public synthetic demonstration from a local private portal and API. Inventory and purchasing model explicit state changes, permissions and audit records.
projects.tradeoff: Browser-local demo data makes exploration easy, but cannot provide shared persistence or server authorization. The private API provides a separate path for those concerns.
projects.outcome: The repository documents public demo workflows and a local authenticated portal. Production identity and deployment remain separate work; all demonstration data is fictitious.
projects.lesson: A convincing product includes its operating limits. Showing what is simulated helps a reviewer assess the architecture honestly.

projects.title: Knowledge that ships.
projects.name: DevOps learning lab
projects.summary: One application. An entire delivery lifecycle. A practical way to teach systems thinking.
projects.problem: Teaching tools in isolation makes it difficult to understand how software becomes an operated service.
projects.approach: A single application travels from source control through containers, delivery automation, orchestration, monitoring and security. The course includes bilingual guides and debugging exercises.
projects.tradeoff: A coherent learning path prioritizes a small reproducible environment over the complexity of a production platform. Intentional failure exercises make the limits teachable.
projects.outcome: The repository provides a four-day curriculum, application examples, deployment manifests, instructor material and troubleshooting exercises. Learning outcomes are not inferred from attendance.
projects.lesson: Technical leadership scales through artifacts people can use independently: runnable examples, decision guides and clear recovery paths.
